subject: Stakeholder alignment: private hosting unknowns & ops impacts
messages:
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eva Rosales <eva@edgecloud.io>, Simon Hayes <simon.hayes@northwind.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stakeholder alignment: private hosting unknowns & ops impacts

Team —

Following up from last week's infra sync: Northwind has pushed us on a private hosting proposal (VPC + customer-managed on-prem gateway). Before we give firm timelines, I want to surface the open technical and operational unknowns so product, security, and architecture are aligned. Attachments: vpc-network-draft.pdf (network CIDR proposals) and ops-runbook-draft.md (initial ops checklist).

Primary asks (please reply inline or at latest by EOD Tuesday):
- Architecture: confirm whether we can support a customer-managed NFS/S3 gateway (S3-compatible) or if we need an application-level adapter (owner: Karthik)
- Security: any gating controls (HSM/KMS, cert rotation, pen test) that would move timeline to Q3 or later? (owner: Kimberly)
- Product: feature gating / canary expectations for gradual rollout (owner: Priyom)
- Program: staffing for pilot on-call and incident response (owner: Laura)

Notes: Northwind requires 2 AM - 6 AM local maintenance windows for on-prem patching and expects log retention controls on their side. I've CC'd their PM (Simon) and our integration partner (Eva) to keep visibility.

High-level timeline we discussed with them: pilot kickoff in June, broad availability in Sept if no major blockers. If any owner believes a blocker pushes us out of that window, call it out explicitly.

Thanks —
Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Director, Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

---
(Attachment: vpc-network-draft.pdf, ops-runbook-draft.md)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Eva Rosales <eva@edgecloud.io>, Simon Hayes <simon.hayes@northwind.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stakeholder alignment: private hosting unknowns & ops impacts

Quick read — a couple product clarifications from my side:
- We need explicit canary support: traffic split and rollback hooks at the routing layer. If we can't do routing-level canaries for private installs, product will require a feature flag path which adds dev + QA work.
- Metrics surface: Northwind wants per-tenant token cost visibility. Is that available in private deployments out of the box or do we need to plan a telemetry export?

If either of these looks like a blocker for June pilot, flag now. Otherwise I'll docket a small spec for the canary behavior next week.

— Priyom
Head of Product, Deployment Experience
Redwood Inference

---
(One-line replies welcome)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eva Rosales <eva@edgecloud.io>, Simon Hayes <simon.hayes@northwind.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stakeholder alignment: private hosting unknowns & ops impacts

Thanks Rohan — short take from arch: 
- Network: the vpc-network-draft.pdf looks fine for CIDR and peering. Main unknown is egress control for on-prem gateway: if Northwind wants strict egress NAT + per-service proxy (for auditor), that adds ~2–3 sprint effort (ops + infra) to build and test.
- Storage: supporting an S3-compatible gateway (e.g., MinIO behind a customer gateway) is feasible, but the integration surface is where the unknowns live: multipart upload compatibility for large model artifacts, and consistent object ACLs across gateway and our model cache. We'll need to run a compatibility pass with their appliance.
- KV cache persistence: if ops prefer local SSD-backed caches vs shared NFS, that impacts our rollback and warm-start behavior. Need a decision from Northwind on whether they will expose a shared POSIX store or prefer container-local state.

I'll capture these as short tech spikes. ETA: 1 week for spike + compatibility test plan. Attaching quick notes I took during the sync (will push to the drive).

-Karthik
Principal Architect, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

---
(Inline note: arch spike will include a small test harness to validate multipart uploads and ACL behavior)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eva Rosales <eva@edgecloud.io>, Simon Hayes <simon.hayes@northwind.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stakeholder alignment: private hosting unknowns & ops impacts

Security notes and gating items: 
- KMS/HSM: if Northwind insists on local HSM integration we need a connector and verification window; expect +4 weeks for HSM onboarding and key ceremony coordination (legal + infra + their ops).
- Audit logs: we must ensure immutable logs are exported to a customer-owned endpoint. Our current private agent supports log-forwarding, but retention policies are configurable only via the ops-runbook.
- Pen test / vulnerability scan: we'll require a white-box scan prior to GA and a crash plan for any high/critical findings; this can push GA by ~2–6 weeks depending on severity.
- Compliance: any additional contractual controls (e.g., specific data deletion clauses) need early review by legal — I've looped in our external counsel separately.

Action: Laura, can you add KMS onboarding, pen-test execution, and log retention confirmation to the pilot checklist with owners and expected lead times?

Thanks,
Kimberly
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Simon Hayes <simon.hayes@northwind.com>

Cc: Eva Rosales <eva@edgecloud.io>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stakeholder alignment: private hosting unknowns & ops impacts

Appreciate the clarity — a few clarifications from our side: 
- Maintenance window: the 2 AM - 6 AM window is preferred, but we can negotiate a narrower slot for critical patches. We cannot accept a full-day maintenance period.
- Storage: our appliances will expose an S3-compatible endpoint; we need your artifact push to support server-side encryption (SSE) with customer-provided keys.
- HSM: we do have an HSM and will entertain an integration, but will need a demo of the connector approach before committing.

We can provide a test appliance the week of April 4th for the compatibility spike Karthik mentioned. Eva will coordinate logistics.

Best,
Simon Hayes
Senior PM, Infrastructure
Northwind Energy

- Kimberly: KMS/HSM onboarding checklist and pen-test plan; add gating flags to pilot checklist — due 2027-04-08

Related links: https://drive.redwoodinternal/example/priv-hosting-canvas (working doc) and https://confluence.redwoodinternal/display/PRIV/Runbooks (runbook index).

Rohan
